text:
arya: quick followup idea after the quant RFC: introduce a lightweight per-request 'precision_tier' + a short 'replay_token' handed back by the runtime. sketching here before a formal follow-up RFC.

miguel: what exactly is precision_tier vs precision_profile?

arya: tier is a client-facing declarative hint: e.g. `tier:conservative`, `tier:balanced`, `tier:aggressive`. runtime maps a tier to a concrete precision_profile_id (the profile contains quant bits, kernel choices, and fallbacks).

sven: ok. replay_token? we already talked about repro_contracts elsewhere. how is this different?

arya: replay_token is a compact, immutable token that encodes (profile_id, model_digest, kv_stamp, seed_hint, tier) and a determinism_score. it's friendly for logs and can be exchanged with ops for targeted replay. Not a full JSON blob - just a signed token string you can store in a DB.

chai: signed token means extra crypto on hot path. can we avoid blocking the request?

arya: plan: issue an unsigned short token immediately, then schedule an async signer job that pushes a signed v2 token to telemetry. clients can opt-in to wait for the signed token with a flag if they need it synchronously. default: unsigned short token + later signed token delivered via metadata stream.

miguel: determinism_score? explain.

arya: determinism_score is [0..1] computed from admission facts: whether kv checksum present, if batching used, rng seed fixed, hardware variance (if using tensor cores with mixed FP). 1.0 means highly reproducible; <0.6 we tag `replay.guarantee=none`. score included in token metadata.

sven: admission locking concerns: if a request gets admitted to `tier:aggressive` but route changes mid-flight to a different node with different kernel set, we must avoid mismatches. admission must pin profile_id for lifetime of request.

arya: agreed. admission API sketch: POST /admit {model, prompt_hash, precision_hint?, tier?} -> {admit_id, profile_id, est_cost_multiplier, determinism_score, admit_ttl}. client can call admit and then send request referencing admit_id. runtime enforces pinning.

chai: what about batching autoscaler? if we pin and the node dies, fallback must be graceful. allow fallback profiles only if replicated and signed in admission step, otherwise return an error.

miguel: rollout and telemetry: we should track paired-shadow comparisons. for a sampled subset we run the same request on baseline (fp32/q8) and compute paired metrics: paired_nll_diff, paired_token_mismatch_rate, headwise_confidence_drop. store these with replay_token for traceability.

arya: sampling fraction idea: default 0.5% per-customer, rampable. store sample pairing id in token: `paired_id:shd-xxxx`. Use that to correlate replays.

sven: thresholds / auto actions: propose ruleset: if paired_token_mismatch_rate > 0.025 and paired_samples>200 -> pause tier for that customer. if headwise_confidence_drop>0.10 & hallucination_signals>metric_thresh -> immediate rollback.

chai: billing: if client requested `tier:aggressive` and got cheaper profile, do we bill baseline or adjusted cost? we need transparency.

arya: API returns `applied_cost_multiplier` and `cost_basis_profile`. invoice renderer uses those fields. also include `quality_budget` in admit API: e.g. {max_cost_multiplier:1.1, min_determinism:0.7}. runtime must respect both.

miguel: security/GDPR note: replay_token must not include raw prompt. only store prompt_hash (salted by tenant-provided salt if tenant wants privacy). platform stores nothing that could reverse prompt. replay requires tenant to provide the salt.

sven: signing keys: ops prefers platform KMS-signed tokens (rotateable). tenants can request tenant-key signing but needs onboarding. default is platform-sign + tenant-salt model for audit.

chai: instrumentation cost: signing + paired baseline runs are heavy. we should make signed tokens and paired shadows opt-in per customer until we have cost amortization.

arya: operational flow: 1) client optionally preflight via admit API 2) runtime pins profile_id on admission 3) request runs, immediate lightweight unsigned replay_token returned 4) async signing + telemetry attaches signed token and paired-shadow results later if sampled 5) client can fetch signed token / paired metrics via GET /replay/{token} within TTL.

miguel: TTL and storage: keep replay artifacts for 30 days by default behind retention flags; longer retention as enterprise add-on. store minimal metadata only.

sven: can we ensure atomicity of cache + admission? if prefix cache returns early we may have different kv_stamp than admission expected. admission should include snapshot of prefix_mode (none/full/partial) and admission must take a lightweight kv_snapshot_id.

arya: yes: include kv_snapshot_id in admit response. runtime will compute kv_checksum in background and update token status once checksum available. if kv_snapshot_id is missing then determinism_score drops.

chai: ops automation: deploy-bot can implement rule templates.

deploy-bot: rule template available: `pause-tier if (paired_token_mismatch_rate > 0.025 && paired_samples >= 200)`. can attach to rollout pipelines. :robot_face:

miguel: docs + UX: we should keep client model simple: most users use tier only, advanced users use admit+quality_budget. examples in SDK.

sven: action items: arya draft RFC with admit API, token schema (v1 unsigned, v2 signed), determinism_score calc, sampling plan, rollout automation, and telemetry metrics + thresholds. miguel to review telemetry, chai to review ops/keying, sven to review admission+kv snapshot plan.

arya: will write today and ping reviewers. filing RFC link here when ready.

deploy-bot: added calendar reminder: "Precision tier admit API RFC review" in eng-ml tomorrow 09:30 UTC.
